# Mixed advanced contest habits

At this level, the danger is applying a powerful tool before the problem model
has earned it.

# Complete twelve-problem set

The virtual contest contains twelve problems. A--F establish the broad core;
G--L are ordered as a progressively harder second half:

| Category | Problem package |
|---|---|
| String Algorithms I | E. Pattern Prefix Matches |
| String Algorithms II | F. Suffix LCP Queries |
| Flows and Matchings | G. Domino Placement |
| Rerooting and Advanced Tree DP | H. Weighted Tree Distances |
| Meet-in-the-Middle | I. Balanced Subset Difference |
| Divide-and-Conquer DP Optimization | J. Monge Partition Table |
| Convex Hull Trick and Li Chao Tree | K. Online Line DP |
| Min-cost flow synthesis | L. Profitable Disjoint Routes |

All twelve packages are local and contain statements, stubs, references, and
tests. The checker runs A--L.

# Diagnose the mathematical object

For every local task, write a short model before coding:

```text
What is the state, relation, or algebraic constraint?
Which quantities are invariant under the allowed operations?
Can the input be split into independent parts or reduced recursively?
What makes a candidate answer valid?
```

Then derive a small case by hand and compare it with the proposed model. Do
not use the local statements as labels for known algorithms; the editorial is
where their final reductions belong.

# Proof checkpoints

An advanced solution needs a proof of the transformation as well as a proof of
the algorithm. Check that every original solution maps to a constructed object
and every constructed object maps back. For a recurrence, prove base cases and
the split. For a modular condition, verify existence and uniqueness assumptions
before combining constraints.

# Implementation and testing

Use types large enough for intermediate products, normalize modular values, and
make base cases explicit. Write a deliberately slow oracle for very small input
when possible. Test neutral elements, repeated constraints, impossible cases,
and maximum bit lengths separately.

# Exercises

Attempt all twelve problems by recording the model, the key proof
obligation, and a tiny counterexample that would disprove your idea. Read each
source section's editorial only after that written attempt.
